scoring_rules.a_prior_is_scored_on_its_stated_content: A prior that names a mechanism is scored on that mechanism, not on its genus. A prior scored on its genus cannot be lost, and a prior that cannot be lost measures nothing.
scoring_rules.split_priors: Where a prior's consequent and its stated mechanism diverge, both are scored and the headline score is the more informative of the two. Sub-scores are always carried.
scoring_rules.live_prediction_flag: was_a_live_prediction is false when the answer was already present in a record available to the plan's author or to the reader before the reader derived it. A non-live confirmation is corroboration, not a test, and must not be counted when measuring this Coordinator's calibration.
scoring_rules.who_established_it: Each entry records whether the score rests on a reader verdict, on a machine-checkable artifact, or on a Coordinator inference from reader-established facts. Coordinator inferences are marked and are checkable by any later reader; they are not reader verdicts.

priors.claim: Semaev 2015/310's statement is stronger than his argument delivers, in the specific sense that the argument bounds the quantity at a fixed or typical instance while the statement quantifies over all instances.
priors.reasoning: The reader finds the OPPOSITE about the argument: its quantifier order is the strongest available -- a single uniform witness good for all n, all V, all B, all non-terminal links, and explicitly 'not a per-instance witness dressed up as a uniform one' (B-2). The gap is real but of a different shape: QUANTITY (fake vs true degree; d_ff vs d_F4) and COVERAGE (t-2 of t-1 equations, so one is uncovered at every t, and the count is zero at t = 2, which Assumption 1's range includes). A quantifier slide does exist, but in the experimental SUPPORT for Assumption 1, which is not the argument P-5 was about.

priors.claim: The numbering mismatch in P-1 has a mundane explanation rather than being a miscitation: the served 2013/549 PDF is the last of two revisions, whose own note records deleting the content of Section 4; deleting content plausibly renumbered the lemmas, so 'Lemma 3' may be correct for the version Nagao cited.
priors.reasoning: The proposed mechanism cannot have produced this mismatch, and the served text shows the author did not renumber at all. (a) Lemma 2 is in Section 2 (pymupdf 303) while the deletion was of Section 4 content (pymupdf 35); a later deletion cannot shift an earlier statement's number. (b) The served numbering runs Lemma 1..9, then Lemma 11, 12, 13 -- a hole at 10. A paper that leaves a hole after deleting content did not renumber, it left gaps. So no statement shifted and Lemma 2 was Lemma 2 in the first revision too.
priors.established_by: COORDINATOR INFERENCE from two reader-established facts plus one direct check of a frozen file by this task. Not a reader verdict.
